concepts.name: state
concepts.description: A configuration in a state space.

concepts.name: configuration
concepts.description: A representation of the arrangement of objects in a problem.

concepts.name: difference
concepts.description: A discrepancy between a current state and a goal state.

concepts.name: heuristic
concepts.description: A rule of thumb used to guide search from the initial state toward the goal state by estimating which operator or state is most promising.

concepts.name: operator
concepts.description: An action that transforms one state into another.

concepts.name: stateSpace
concepts.description: The set of all states that can be generated by applying operators.

concepts.name: comparison
concepts.description: A representation of similarities and differences between states.

concepts.name: ProblemReduction
concepts.description: A problem-solving method that decomposes a difficult problem into smaller subproblems or subgoals.

concepts.name: Subgoal
concepts.description: A smaller goal produced by decomposing a larger goal during problem reduction.

concepts.name: UniversalMethod
concepts.description: A general-purpose problem-solving method that can apply across a broad class of problems.

concepts.name: WeakMethod
concepts.description: A heuristic or strategy that guides problem solving without guaranteeing an optimal or complete solution.

concepts.name: StrongMethod
concepts.description: A knowledge-intensive problem-solving method that uses substantial domain knowledge to produce solutions efficiently.

concepts.name: InitialState
concepts.description: The starting configuration of a problem before any operators are applied.

concepts.name: GoalState
concepts.description: The desired target configuration that the problem solver aims to achieve.

values.description: Goal state achieved after reducing differences.
Blocks World example used to illustrate means-ends analysis.
Raven's Progressive Matrices problem represented as state transformations.

assertions.name: goodSolution
assertions.description: A solution is good when repeated operator application reduces differences until the goal state is reached.
